annotations.annotation_text: Egyptian eschatology "set" on page 138 ("The Quiz Chapter"): within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones, HCE appears as the dismembered Osiris and ALP as Isis gathering his scattered limbs. Mark Troy's research traces how Joyce embedded the Papyrus of Ani's resurrection liturgy throughout this Age of Gods passage — the dream-journey through the underworld (Tuat) toward solar rebirth.

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "porter" on page 138 ("The Quiz Chapter"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 138 ("The Quiz Chapter"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. During this Age of Gods phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
